chunks: 36 - Muhammad ibn Uthman narrated: Al-Muqaddami narrated from Aasim ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Miqdam who narrated from his father, from Fitr ibn Khaleefa, from Abu Khalid al-Walibi, who said: Jabir ibn Samra narrated to us that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying:
This matter (the religion/leadership) will remain prominent; the one who opposes it will not harm it, until there are twelve Caliphs, all of them from Quraysh.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of caliphs and their tribe?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani in *Kitab al-Ghayba*, serves as a primary textual proof (hujjah) for the number and Qurayshi lineage of the Twelve Imams, with the 'caliphs' (khulafa') interpreted by Shia scholars as divinely appointed successors rather than merely political rulers. The phrase 'those who oppose it will not harm it' underscores the infallibility and enduring authority of the Imams throughout history. This narration is frequently cited alongside the Hadith of Twelve Caliphs in Sunni sources to demonstrate the universality of this specific succession model.
